newsitem.title: FINLAND: Nokia upbeat on German D box market - paper.
newsitem.headline: Nokia upbeat on German D box market - paper.

text.p: Finnish telecoms group Nokia sees excellent business prospects for its digital TV decoder, or D box, in Germany, where operators have set the stage for a big launch, daily Helsingin Sanomat reported on Thursday.
"It will mean extremely good business," the paper quoted Nokia Multimedia Network Terminals' managing director Heikki Koskinen as saying.
He said German telecoms group Deutsche Telekom had accepted Nokia's multimedia terminal as its digital television decoder.
Helsingin Sanomat said Deutsche Telekom owns the German cable network used by its own five million subscribers and by the other cable operators' 10 million viewers.
Koskinen said Nokia would be the only provider of terminals in Germany, where operators aim to make digital programming widely available before Christmas, but gave no business volume estimate.
"We are the sole provider. The entire German digitalisation in satellite as well as in cable rely on this technology," Koskinen said.

Bavarian tycoon Leo Kirch's digital TV operator Kirch and its rival Bertelsmann last week agreed to split French Canal Plus' pay-TV company Premiere, in a move which helped push the German digitalisation project forward.
Nokia has developed its decoder in cooperation with Kirch and has an agreement to supply one million terminals.
"In this sort of business, nobody else has such long-term orders," he said. "The situation is quite unique," he said.
